272999727977a642.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Several things of one kind to scan and tap individually, even when asked to tap just one of them. Not one featured thing (Card), details of one thing (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: A plain roster of people: several participants, teammates, clients or family members, with names and optional photos or roles. Choose this even for just names and photos, without roles, links or turn controls. Not general non-person records (List) or one person's identity block (Profile).
- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. Pick: Several measured amounts, each against its own target, such as macros, a budget per category or lessons per course. Not one main goal (Ring), amounts compared with each other (Bars), or place in a short sequence (Steps).
- Ring: How far you are toward one goal. Pick: One amount completed toward a target. Not several targets at once (Progress), several summary numbers (Stats) or ordered stages of a process (Steps).
- Route: Follow a path between places, from the first stop to the last. Pick: Show places visited in travel order, with an optional total distance. Not events ordered by time (Timeline) or locations positioned on a map without a visiting order (MapPins).
- Scale: Log a rating or feeling from one to five. Pick: Rate how something went, feels or looks on five ordered levels. Not switching views (Segmented) or entering information in a general input (Field).
- Search: Find one thing among many by typing words from its name. Pick: Type a query above a list to find matching things. Not a few fixed filters (Chips), entering one piece of information (Field) or writing several lines (Composer).
- SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).
- Stats: Two to four independent summary numbers, with labels, units and optional change arrows. Pick: Several independent summary measurements shown together, with an optional change arrow on each. Not amounts compared across days or categories (Bars), one latest measurement with its recent line (Sparkline), one record's details (KeyValue), one headline number (Hero), or one sum of money (Amount).
- Steps: Know your current place in a short ordered flow. Pick: Show the current position in a short setup or booking flow. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist) or progress toward a numeric goal (Ring).
- Streak: How many days in a row you kept a habit, with this week's completed days. Pick: Consecutive days of a habit with daily completion this week. Not several independent totals (Stats) or your position in an ordered flow (Steps).
- Success: Know an action worked, with its result and the saved item's details. Pick: A standalone moment after an action worked, with a result title and optional detail. Not an ongoing status or urgent warning at the top (Banner), or a screen with no content yet (Empty).
- SwipeStack: Choose between things one at a time, swiping the current one to keep or skip. Pick: Decide which of several things to keep or skip, one at a time. Swipe only the top choice. Not browsing several captioned pictures together (Gallery) or opening a single featured preview (Card).
- Timeline: Events in time order, or activities sized by duration on an hour rail. Pick: Dated or timed events in order. Use hours when start/end times, duration and free gaps matter. Not choosing dates (Calendar), things without times to browse (List), or independent jobs (Checklist).
- Timer: Measure time remaining or elapsed, with controls to start and stop. Pick: Time remaining until an activity ends or elapsed since it began. Not a number manually nudged up or down (Counter) or an amount completed toward a goal (Ring).
- Approval: Review staff requests and decide whether to approve or decline them. Pick: A manager decides on submitted staff requests such as time off, swaps and expenses. Not jobs to tick off (Checklist) or a client accepting a quote (Invoice).
- Handover: Read what the last shift passed on and mark each note as seen. Pick: Read shift-to-shift notes with author, time, optional flag and a mark-as-seen control. Not writing your own note (Composer), chatting (Bubbles), or a record change log (ActivityLog).
- OpenShift: Pick up an unassigned shift and see when it runs and what it pays. Pick: Claim one of several unassigned work shifts with a date, time range, role and optional pay. Not an assigned shift (Shift) or a list of jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- Roster: See who works each day this week and spot gaps in cover. Pick: A weekly grid comparing staff shift times across people and days. Not one person's daily schedule (Timeline), one shift (Shift), bookable hours (Availability), a sports lineup (Lineup), or class periods (Timetable).
- Shift: See one assigned shift and ask to swap it or offer it to someone else. Pick: One assigned staff shift with start and end times, coworkers and swap or offer actions. Not a record preview (Card), the whole rota (Roster), or a client's booking (Appointment).
- TimeClock: Clock in and out of a work shift and record breaks. Pick: Record work attendance with clock-in, clock-out and breaks for the current shift. Not a stopwatch or countdown for an activity (Timer), or approving a week's hours (Timesheet).
- Timesheet: Review and approve the hours each person worked during a week. Pick: Review each worker's actual hours for seven days and approve their weekly row. Not a chart of daily totals (Bars), a planned rota (Roster), or a generic table (Table).

Need, in the person's words: "Show the unassigned work shifts, their hours and pay, with a button to claim each shift."
Reply with only the component id, nothing else.

- beauty: Personal skincare and haircare routines, opened-product shelf life, ingredient and skin-type checks, beauty profiles and saved shade lookbooks. Pick: Use for managing a personal beauty regimen. Not buying products (commerce), booking salon visits (booking), or virtual AR try-on (core).

Booking alone covers clients booking a provider's appointments or studio classes; clients, providers, paid services and class groups do not imply customers, team, commerce, events or community. Add another pack only for an explicitly requested separate job. Not selling goods (commerce). Reply only with a valid JSON array of pack ids, never an object, invented app name or explanation.
- books: Keeping a small business's books: record money received and spent, retain receipts, separate business costs from owner withdrawals, and understand a period's profit and tax provision. The default is local cash-basis bookkeeping for one business, not banking, certified accounts or automatic tax filing. Pick: A small business's own accounts: income, expenses, profit, tax set aside. Not personal money (money), client invoices (customers), or selling goods (commerce)
- comics: Webtoons and manga: read sequential panels, follow series on a shelf, see weekly release calendars and unlock serialized chapters with coins or wait timers. Pick: Use for sequential visual storytelling and chapter gates. Not prose books or audio (media), or simply showing standalone illustrations (core).
- commerce: Goods on offer, a basket, an order and its progress, from both sides: the buyer browsing and ordering, and the seller seeing orders come in, moving them on and keeping products up to date. It covers small sellers (a bakery taking pre-orders, a market stall, a maker selling prints). Taking payment is always a service part. Pick: Selling things for money: a shop, a bakery, a stall. Not booking time (booking)
- comms: Direct and workplace communication across chat and email threads, server channels, contacts, and voice or video calls. Pick: Multi-thread inboxes, channel navigation, call lobbies, voicemail and T9 dialing. Member subscriptions and spending votes are governance, not personal finance (money); member sign-ups are not appointments (booking). Not sharing posts (social), not organising one gathering (events), not staff shifts (team)

- customers: Keep a business's client records, history, invoices, reviews, rewards and signed agreements. Rule: Use style "back" only when a back button is needed. To hide a subtitle, use detail "brief" and keep the supplied subtitle in sub. Hiding it does not request a smaller title or a denser header: set emphasis and density to null unless the brief explicitly asks for those changes.

49d4d73b34e93004.prompt:
Choose the domain packs this app needs from the index below. For each independently requested workflow choose only its most specific matching pack. Do not add overlapping packs or infer workflows from incidental details. Include a matching domain even for a private, single-screen app or when core components cover some screens. Choose [] only if no domain matches.

- assistant: Conversations with an AI: streaming answers and code, cited sources, tool traces, generated artifacts, starter prompts and voice mode. Pick: Use assistant alone for an AI chat that accepts notes and generates guides or other artifacts. Add workspace only for independent file sharing or editing, and media only for a separately managed reading library. Not human chat (comms) or graded quizzes (learning).
- auto: Cars and EVs: a vehicle garage, remote controls, mileage-based maintenance, OBD diagnostics, charging and fill-ups, parking meters, and used-car listings with VIN reports. Pick: Pick for operating, maintaining, charging, parking or shopping for vehicles. A used-car shortlist with VIN reports is auto alone, not an owned-asset catalog (inventory). Not turn-by-turn guidance (navigation), home automation (home), or a map of venues or stations (places).
- beauty: Personal skincare and haircare routines, opened-product shelf life, ingredient and skin-type checks, beauty profiles and saved shade lookbooks. Pick: Use for managing a personal beauty regimen. Not buying products (commerce), booking salon visits (booking), or virtual AR try-on (core).
- booking: Offer services and book appointments, classes and free start times. Pick: Booking time with someone: appointments, classes, slots and class waitlists. Booking alone covers clients booking a provider's appointments or studio classes; clients, providers, paid services and class groups do not imply customers, team, commerce, events or community. Add another pack only for an explicitly requested separate job. Not selling goods (commerce). Reply only with a valid JSON array of pack ids, never an object, invented app name or explanation.
- books: Keeping a small business's books: record money received and spent, retain receipts, separate business costs from owner withdrawals, and understand a period's profit and tax provision. The default is local cash-basis bookkeeping for one business, not banking, certified accounts or automatic tax filing. Pick: A small business's own accounts: income, expenses, profit, tax set aside. Not personal money (money), client invoices (customers), or selling goods (commerce)
- comics: Webtoons and manga: read sequential panels, follow series on a shelf, see weekly release calendars and unlock serialized chapters with coins or wait timers. Pick: Use for sequential visual storytelling and chapter gates. Not prose books or audio (media), or simply showing standalone illustrations (core).
- commerce: Goods on offer, a basket, an order and its progress, from both sides: the buyer browsing and ordering, and the seller seeing orders come in, moving them on and keeping products up to date. It covers small sellers (a bakery taking pre-orders, a market stall, a maker selling prints). Taking payment is always a service part. Pick: Selling things for money: a shop, a bakery, a stall. Not booking time (booking)
- comms: Direct and workplace communication across chat and email threads, server channels, contacts, and voice or video calls. Pick: Multi-thread inboxes, channel navigation, call lobbies, voicemail and T9 dialing. Not one simple conversation (core), public feeds (social), club governance (community), or service tickets (requests).
- community: The continuing work of a member-run group: who belongs and can vote, subscriptions collected by the treasurer, motions decided under the group's rules, contributions people claim, and the agreed record of decisions and actions. Notices use the core; this pack adds governance, not another social feed. Pick: A club, association or neighbourhood group run by its members: dues, notices, votes, sign-ups, minutes. Member subscriptions and spending votes are governance, not personal finance (money); member sign-ups are not appointments (booking). Not sharing posts (social), not organising one gathering (events), not staff shifts (team)
- curation: Collect visual inspiration in staggered pin grids, inspect sources and palettes, build shared moodboards and flatlay collages, and discover preferred styles. Pick: Use for gathering inspiration, not editing photos (studio), shopping a catalog (commerce), or tracking owned items (inventory).
- customers: Keep a business's client records, history, invoices, reviews, rewards and signed agreements. Pick: A client book: keep records about clients, such as profiles, visit history and notes, consent, agreements, client invoices, reviews and loyalty. Choose customers for a client-records job, not because another workflow has customers or records transactions. Buying goods and checking out are commerce; reserving appointments is booking. Friends sharing posts, comments and follows belong to social.
- data: The back office of a small operation: many records at once, sorted and filtered, moved through stages, changed in bulk, and summarised in charts. Any pack component allowed by the README's density rule may be dense. Pick: Running something behind the scenes: tables, boards, reports. Not personal tracking (core)
- dating: Romantic matching: relationship profiles, mutual likes, expiring match queues, compatibility, icebreakers and safety check-ins for dates. Pick: Use for finding or meeting a match, not public posts (social), ordinary direct messages (comms), or simple swipe cards (core).
- dining: Restaurant and café customer flows: dietary menus, configurable dishes, curbside or drive-through check-in, tables and walk-in queues, and diner points rewards. Pick: Use for dining out, configurable restaurant orders or a restaurant's tables and walk-in queue. Restaurant reservations and waitlists alone do not need booking or places. Not meals cooked at home (kitchen), ordinary bakery or shop pre-orders (commerce), or a business's client book (customers).
- dispatch: Independent courier or gig driver operations: go online by zone, accept timed offers, verify pickup and dropoff, and see shift payout breakdowns. Pick: Use for a worker handling live delivery jobs, not staff rosters (team), customer parcel maps (places), passenger ride tracking (navigation), or bookkeeping (books).
- events: Running one event from the organiser's side and the guest's: who is invited and coming, what they will eat, where they sit, who supplies what and what it costs, tickets and the door on the day, the gift list, and finding a date that suits everyone. Weddings, parties, reunions, fundraisers, small conferences. Pick: Organising one gathering: guests, RSVPs, seating, tickets, suppliers, gifts. Not travel (trips)
- fantasy: Fantasy leagues and player-stat contests: snake drafts, fantasy lineups, waiver bids, live fantasy matchups, prop picks, odds boards and pick slips. Pick: Use when managers draft real players into fantasy rosters or predict player outcomes. Not running a real sports league (sports), or a casual tabletop game (play).
- health: The most-asked personal app family: logging workouts set by set, taking medication on time, watching a body measurement move toward a goal, keeping several healthy habits, tracking symptoms, vitals and a menstrual cycle. Everything stays on the phone; nothing here is medical advice, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The body: workouts, medication, measurements, symptoms, cycles. Not the mind (mind), not food (kitchen)
- hiring: Before someone joins a team, a small employer tracks openings and applicants, reviews evidence, arranges interviews and records offers. A job seeker tracks the same process from the other side. Both can keep records on one phone; this pack does not promise a job board, shared recruiting system or automatic hiring. Pick: Finding people or work: job posts, applicants, interviews, offers and your own applications. Not staff already hired (team), not clients (customers), not a generic kanban (data)
- home: The work of a home shared among the people in it: chores and whose turn it is, rewards for kids, the family's week, recurring care for pets, plants, the car and the house, a baby's feeds and sleeps, and the devices in the rooms, including set points, one-tap scenes and sensor readings. Pick: Running a household: chores, family, pets, plants, cars, the house and its devices. Not a business team (team)
- inventory: Knowing what you have, where it is, who has it, when its warranty ends and what you still want, from a garage of boxes to a small shop's stock room, a record collection or a few rental flats. For rentals it covers the listing, the lease and a single rental-repair summary only; any request workflow (queue, triage, thread, work order) belongs to the requests pack. The tenants themselves are customers. Pick: Keeping track of things owned: stock, collections, storage, loans, warranties, rentals. Not selling them (commerce)
- invest: Following money set aside for the future: what is owned, how its value changes apart from contributions, what income it pays, and how close it brings a savings target. It records investments, not advice or orders to a broker. A first showcase uses local records and dated quotes; live prices need a service. Pick: Investments over time: holdings, allocation, watchlists, performance, dividends, savings goals. Not day-to-day spending and bills (money), not a business's books (books, proposed)
- kids: Child-facing experiences for pre-readers: profile avatars, sounds and phonics, illustrated read-alongs, stickers, visual routines and parent gates. Pick: Use kids alone for a young child's icon-first experience, even when an adult unlocks settings or the child follows a visual routine. Not graded lessons (learning), parent-managed logs and screen limits (parenting), or family chore management (home).
- kitchen: Everything about food in a household: cooking from a recipe with the right amounts and timers, planning the week's meals, the shopping list that follows from it, what is in the cupboard and when it goes off, and a simple log of what was eaten. Pick: Food at home: recipes, meal plans, groceries, the pantry, food logs. Not selling food (commerce)
- learning: Learning something step by step and checking it stuck: lessons, questions with feedback, flashcards with spaced review, a path through units, results and badges, and a student's week of classes and homework. Pick: Teaching and practising: lessons, quizzes, flashcards, classes and homework. Not a team's training rota (team)
- marketplace: Peer-to-peer resale, auctions, negotiated offers, seller bundles, hosted drops and shipping labels for secondhand sellers. Pick: Use marketplace alone for private sellers' secondhand listings, bundles and auctions. Items being offered for resale do not require a stock or possessions catalog (inventory). Not a fixed-price retail storefront (commerce), used-car search (auto), or live-event ticket resale (ticketing).
- media: A library of things to read, hear or watch: articles, books, podcasts, albums, sermons, video courses. The core Player plays one recording; this pack adds what a library needs around it: the reading view, a show's page, episode lists, chapters, a player that follows the person between screens, and saved highlights. Pick: Reading, listening and watching a library. Not one recording on one screen (core Player)
- medical: Patient portal, pharmacy and clinical workflows: lab reference ranges, prescription refills and prices, telehealth, insurance coverage, care records and connected therapy summaries. No automated diagnosis. Pick: Pick for provider-facing or patient-facing clinical records or care workflows. Not personal exercise, symptom or pill tracking (health), or nonclinical client billing (customers).
- mind: Looking after how one feels: a daily check-in of mood and what affected it, a journal, naming feelings, breathing exercises, sleep, calming sounds, and the patterns that show up over weeks. It is calm by design: soft presets, no red alarms, nothing competitive. Pick: The mind: mood, journaling, feelings, breathing, sleep. Not the body (health)
- money: Personal and household money: what is in each account, where it went, what is due, who owes whom, how to clear debts, and how a holding is doing. It never moves money in a first showcase; bank links and payments are service, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The person's own money: balances, budgets, bills, splitting costs, debts and repayment plans. Not a business's sales (commerce)
- navigation: Active routing and mobility: turn-by-turn and lane guidance, route alternatives, transit legs, road hazards, trail elevation, offline maps and passenger ride tracking. Pick: Use navigation alone to compare routes, follow turn-by-turn directions on bike or foot, or make transit transfers. A destination, stop or hazard on that route does not need places. Choose places only for a separate venue, departure-board or parcel-map workflow. Not holiday itineraries (trips) or a driver's job offers (dispatch).
- news: Follow journalism and developing stories with attributed headlines, comparisons across outlets, live blogs, breaking tickers, daily digests and publisher follows. Pick: Use for discovering and following current reporting, not personal updates (social), a personal library of already saved newsletters, books or audio (media), or an enduring encyclopedia (reference).
- paperwork: IDs, insurance, tax evidence, certificates and personal contracts, with action dates and proof files. The pack is a local filing cabinet, not a bank, travel wallet, warranty book or client-consent workflow. Its hand-drawn signature pad for personal forms does not promise legally verified e-signing. Pick: Life admin: documents, renewals, receipts, forms to sign and deadlines. Not travel documents (trips), owned things' warranties (inventory), client agreements (customers) or payments to track (money)
- parenting: Parent-facing pregnancy, pediatric growth, co-parenting and child wellbeing: gestational milestones, growth percentiles, custody swaps, child expenses, screen limits and private family albums. Pick: Use for pregnancy, growth, custody or child-specific caregiver workflows. A parent gate for settings in a child-facing app belongs to kids, not parenting. Not household chores, general family routines or a simple baby log (home), or clinical records (medical).
- perks: Multi-merchant cashback offers, verified coupon feeds and points-to-cash progress and redemption. Pick: Use when earning or redeeming offers across merchants is the app's job. - places: Real places and moving between them: a venue's card and opening hours, an address to copy or navigate to, a map with a list beside it, a delivery coming to the door, and the next departures from a stop. - play: Tools for playing around one phone: keep a board game's round scores, roll dice, spin for a random choice, take turns, reveal a trivia answer and split the players into teams. It supports the game at the table, not a general game engine, a sports season or a course. No wagers, prizes for money or payments. Pick: Playing a game together: round scores, dice, a spinner, turns, host-led trivia and random teams. Not league fixtures and standings (sports), not graded practice (learning), not household duties (home)
- projects: Delivering a bounded piece of work: agree what is included, break it into assigned tasks, meet milestone gates, see dependencies across dates, and record the time spent on each task. It serves one person managing their own work first; collaborators and clients do not have to use the app. Pick: Work with deliverables: projects, tasks, milestones, time spent. Not running day-to-day operations (data), not staff shifts (team)
- property: The operating view of rented homes: which independently lettable units are occupied, who owes rent for which period, who is viewing, what condition each room was in, and how meters changed. A landlord or host can keep these records on one phone; tenant accounts, automatic payments and booking-platform sync are not implied. This pack does not replace inventory's Lease or Listing. Pick: Landlord operations: rental units, dated occupancy, rent charges and receipts, viewings, inspections and meters. Use property alone for those operations. Add inventory for separately requested listings, leases or owned assets, and money for separate personal finances. Not repair and maintenance queues (requests)
- puzzles: Playable solo puzzles: five-letter word guesses with colored clues, Sudoku with pencil marks, logic and tile grids, and lifeline trivia. Pick: Choose puzzles even for one private daily word game or Sudoku. Guess distributions, streaks and daily cadence are part of the puzzle, not separate domains. Not group or host-led trivia and board games (play), or coursework and exam drills (learning).
- realestate: Home buying and apartment hunting: price-pin maps, property listings, comparison and saved alerts, mortgage affordability and arranging tours. Pick: Use for a buyer or renter searching for a home. Not operating occupied rental units (property), storing one signed lease (inventory), or everyday budgeting (money).
- reference: Read canonical or structured reference material: scripture verse lookup, study plans, parallel translations, dictionary senses and pronunciation, and cited encyclopedia articles. Pick: Use for looking up words, verses or facts. Not consuming general books or audio (media), graded study (learning), or accounting (books).
- requests: An operator takes a reported problem through triage, assigned work, updates and verified resolution. Reports can span visits, have several work orders, wait for parts or information, and reopen after a failed fix. Pick: Requests moving through a service queue: repairs, maintenance, support tickets, work orders. Not booking time (booking), not a simple repair attached to something owned (inventory), not arbitrary records on a board (data)
- rpg: Tabletop role-playing character sheets and encounters: abilities, modifiers, hit points, conditions, spell slots, dice macros, initiative and gear. Pick: Use for pen-and-paper RPG campaigns and encounters. Not standalone dice and game-night score pads (play), or real-time video games (core).
- safety: Personal safety across a trusted circle: live locations, place arrival alerts, safe-driving summaries, hold-to-send SOS and timed check-ins with escalation. Pick: Use for a person's or group's location safety. Not venue and delivery tracking (places), routing (navigation), generic household routines (home), or child screen limits (parenting).
- security: Account and connection protection: rotating 2FA codes, MFA approvals, password and passkey vaults, password generators, recovery codes, VPN controls and credential audits. Pick: Pick for securing sign-ins or connections. Not filing life-admin documents (paperwork) or checking connection speed (utilities).
- social: A small community in one app: a club, a class, a neighbourhood, friends with a shared hobby. People post, react, comment, vote, join challenges and events, and invite others. - sports: Amateur and grassroots sport, run by volunteers: the next match and who is available, the lineup, keeping the score live, what happened in the match, the league table and a knockout cup. It works for any sport with sides, scores and fixtures; football is the default for positions and periods. Pick: A sports team or league: fixtures, scores, standings, lineups, availability. Not a workout (health)
- stays: Shop for lodging and travel fares before booking: compare nightly prices, fare calendars, room rates, amenities and cancellation policies, and watch for price drops. Pick: Use stays alone for pre-booking fare searches and lodging shortlists. Use trips instead for keeping confirmations, packing or an itinerary. Not appointments and class slots (booking).
- studio: Structured visual creation: photo contact sheets, before-and-after wipes, filter presets, brand kits, graphic templates, AI image or video prompt desks and export queues. Pick: Use for transforming photos or producing visual assets. Not a consumption library (media), inspiration pinboards (curation), or freehand and multitrack editors (core).
- team: A small group that works together on a schedule: who is on when, who can cover a gap, hours worked, what the last shift handed over, and requests waiting for a manager. - watch: Television, film and cinema: multi-season catalogs, live TV guides, resume queues, TV remotes, cinema showtimes and auditorium seat selection. Not weather as one detail of a trip itinerary (trips), or venue discovery (places).
- workspace: Shared cloud files and folders, quick notes, versioned team wikis and document review with link and role permissions. Pick: Use when people organize or collaborate on cloud documents or structured wiki pages. Not local files (utilities), personal life-admin records (paperwork), or published books (media).

49e6854891f63f04.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).

Layout: approvals/request. Job: Requests and hours.

Brief: Show Request time off, a choice between Day off and Shift swap, two date fields From and To each set to 2026-11-23, a multiline entry labelled Note with hint Add a note for your manager, then a Send request button.
Return compact JSON. When a layout says to omit a field the schema requires, write null for it instead.

Match every required slot in order. Variants such as shelf, reply, month or mood are the component's style; Field/Camera variants are kind. prices means every Choice option has a price value; toggle means every List row has trail: toggle.

Screen rules: three to nine components outside overlays, total weight at most twelve, at most two weight-three components. One primary Button at most. Hero first in the body; a SectionTitle needs following content. Repeated types cannot be adjacent except Card and Field. Reply Composer is last after Bubbles. 641817dde2aa36f6.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Several things of one kind to scan and tap individually, even when asked to tap just one of them. Not one featured thing (Card), details of one thing (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: A plain roster of people: several participants, teammates, clients or family members, with names and optional photos or roles. Choose this even for just names and photos, without roles, links or turn controls. Not general non-person records (List) or one person's identity block (Profile).
- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. Pick: Several measured amounts, each against its own target, such as macros, a budget per category or lessons per course. Not one main goal (Ring), amounts compared with each other (Bars), or place in a short sequence (Steps).
- Ring: How far you are toward one goal. Pick: One amount completed toward a target. Not several targets at once (Progress), several summary numbers (Stats) or ordered stages of a process (Steps).
- Route: Follow a path between places, from the first stop to the last. Pick: Show places visited in travel order, with an optional total distance. Not events ordered by time (Timeline) or locations positioned on a map without a visiting order (MapPins).
- Scale: Log a rating or feeling from one to five. Pick: Rate how something went, feels or looks on five ordered levels. Not switching views (Segmented) or entering information in a general input (Field).
- Search: Find one thing among many by typing words from its name. Pick: Type a query above a list to find matching things. Not a few fixed filters (Chips), entering one piece of information (Field) or writing several lines (Composer).
- SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).
- Stats: Two to four independent summary numbers, with labels, units and optional change arrows. Pick: Several independent summary measurements shown together, with an optional change arrow on each. Not amounts compared across days or categories (Bars), one latest measurement with its recent line (Sparkline), one record's details (KeyValue), one headline number (Hero), or one sum of money (Amount).
- Steps: Know your current place in a short ordered flow. Pick: Show the current position in a short setup or booking flow. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist) or progress toward a numeric goal (Ring).
- Streak: How many days in a row you kept a habit, with this week's completed days. Pick: Consecutive days of a habit with daily completion this week. Not several independent totals (Stats) or your position in an ordered flow (Steps).
- Success: Know an action worked, with its result and the saved item's details. Pick: A standalone moment after an action worked, with a result title and optional detail. Not an ongoing status or urgent warning at the top (Banner), or a screen with no content yet (Empty).
- SwipeStack: Choose between things one at a time, swiping the current one to keep or skip. Pick: Decide which of several things to keep or skip, one at a time. Swipe only the top choice. Not browsing several captioned pictures together (Gallery) or opening a single featured preview (Card).
- Timeline: Events in time order, or activities sized by duration on an hour rail. Pick: Dated or timed events in order. Use hours when start/end times, duration and free gaps matter. Not choosing dates (Calendar), things without times to browse (List), or independent jobs (Checklist).
- Timer: Measure time remaining or elapsed, with controls to start and stop. Pick: Time remaining until an activity ends or elapsed since it began. Not a number manually nudged up or down (Counter) or an amount completed toward a goal (Ring).
- Approval: Review staff requests and decide whether to approve or decline them. Pick: A manager decides on submitted staff requests such as time off, swaps and expenses. Not jobs to tick off (Checklist) or a client accepting a quote (Invoice).
- Handover: Read what the last shift passed on and mark each note as seen. Pick: Read shift-to-shift notes with author, time, optional flag and a mark-as-seen control. Not writing your own note (Composer), chatting (Bubbles), or a record change log (ActivityLog).
- OpenShift: Pick up an unassigned shift and see when it runs and what it pays. Pick: Claim one of several unassigned work shifts with a date, time range, role and optional pay. Not an assigned shift (Shift) or a list of jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- Roster: See who works each day this week and spot gaps in cover. Pick: A weekly grid comparing staff shift times across people and days. Not one person's daily schedule (Timeline), one shift (Shift), bookable hours (Availability), a sports lineup (Lineup), or class periods (Timetable).
- Shift: See one assigned shift and ask to swap it or offer it to someone else. Pick: One assigned staff shift with start and end times, coworkers and swap or offer actions. Not a record preview (Card), the whole rota (Roster), or a client's booking (Appointment).
- TimeClock: Clock in and out of a work shift and record breaks. Pick: Record work attendance with clock-in, clock-out and breaks for the current shift. Not a stopwatch or countdown for an activity (Timer), or approving a week's hours (Timesheet).
- Timesheet: Review and approve the hours each person worked during a week. Pick: Review each worker's actual hours for seven days and approve their weekly row. Not a chart of daily totals (Bars), a planned rota (Roster), or a generic table (Table).

- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).

bb44bfde16777fdc.prompt:
Choose the domain packs this app needs from the index below. For each independently requested workflow choose only its most specific matching pack. Do not add overlapping packs or infer workflows from incidental details. Include a matching domain even for a private, single-screen app or when core components cover some screens. Choose [] only if no domain matches.

- assistant: Conversations with an AI: streaming answers and code, cited sources, tool traces, generated artifacts, starter prompts and voice mode. Pick: Use assistant alone for an AI chat that accepts notes and generates guides or other artifacts. Add workspace only for independent file sharing or editing, and media only for a separately managed reading library. Not human chat (comms) or graded quizzes (learning).
- auto: Cars and EVs: a vehicle garage, remote controls, mileage-based maintenance, OBD diagnostics, charging and fill-ups, parking meters, and used-car listings with VIN reports. Pick: Pick for operating, maintaining, charging, parking or shopping for vehicles. A used-car shortlist with VIN reports is auto alone, not an owned-asset catalog (inventory). Not turn-by-turn guidance (navigation), home automation (home), or a map of venues or stations (places).
- beauty: Personal skincare and haircare routines, opened-product shelf life, ingredient and skin-type checks, beauty profiles and saved shade lookbooks. Pick: Use for managing a personal beauty regimen. Not buying products (commerce), booking salon visits (booking), or virtual AR try-on (core).
- booking: Offer services and book appointments, classes and free start times. Pick: Booking time with someone: appointments, classes, slots and class waitlists. Booking alone covers clients booking a provider's appointments or studio classes; clients, providers, paid services and class groups do not imply customers, team, commerce, events or community. Add another pack only for an explicitly requested separate job. Not selling goods (commerce). Reply only with a valid JSON array of pack ids, never an object, invented app name or explanation.
- books: Keeping a small business's books: record money received and spent, retain receipts, separate business costs from owner withdrawals, and understand a period's profit and tax provision. The default is local cash-basis bookkeeping for one business, not banking, certified accounts or automatic tax filing. Pick: A small business's own accounts: income, expenses, profit, tax set aside. Not personal money (money), client invoices (customers), or selling goods (commerce)
- comics: Webtoons and manga: read sequential panels, follow series on a shelf, see weekly release calendars and unlock serialized chapters with coins or wait timers. Pick: Use for sequential visual storytelling and chapter gates. Not prose books or audio (media), or simply showing standalone illustrations (core).
- commerce: Goods on offer, a basket, an order and its progress, from both sides: the buyer browsing and ordering, and the seller seeing orders come in, moving them on and keeping products up to date. It covers small sellers (a bakery taking pre-orders, a market stall, a maker selling prints). Taking payment is always a service part. Pick: Selling things for money: a shop, a bakery, a stall. Not booking time (booking)
- comms: Direct and workplace communication across chat and email threads, server channels, contacts, and voice or video calls. Pick: Multi-thread inboxes, channel navigation, call lobbies, voicemail and T9 dialing. Not one simple conversation (core), public feeds (social), club governance (community), or service tickets (requests).
- community: The continuing work of a member-run group: who belongs and can vote, subscriptions collected by the treasurer, motions decided under the group's rules, contributions people claim, and the agreed record of decisions and actions. Notices use the core; this pack adds governance, not another social feed. Pick: A club, association or neighbourhood group run by its members: dues, notices, votes, sign-ups, minutes. Member subscriptions and spending votes are governance, not personal finance (money); member sign-ups are not appointments (booking). Not sharing posts (social), not organising one gathering (events), not staff shifts (team)
- curation: Collect visual inspiration in staggered pin grids, inspect sources and palettes, build shared moodboards and flatlay collages, and discover preferred styles. Pick: Use for gathering inspiration, not editing photos (studio), shopping a catalog (commerce), or tracking owned items (inventory).
- customers: Keep a business's client records, history, invoices, reviews, rewards and signed agreements. Pick: A client book: keep records about clients, such as profiles, visit history and notes, consent, agreements, client invoices, reviews and loyalty. Choose customers for a client-records job, not because another workflow has customers or records transactions. Buying goods and checking out are commerce; reserving appointments is booking. Friends sharing posts, comments and follows belong to social.
- data: The back office of a small operation: many records at once, sorted and filtered, moved through stages, changed in bulk, and summarised in charts. Any pack component allowed by the README's density rule may be dense. Pick: Running something behind the scenes: tables, boards, reports. Not personal tracking (core)
- dating: Romantic matching: relationship profiles, mutual likes, expiring match queues, compatibility, icebreakers and safety check-ins for dates. Pick: Use for finding or meeting a match, not public posts (social), ordinary direct messages (comms), or simple swipe cards (core).
- dining: Restaurant and café customer flows: dietary menus, configurable dishes, curbside or drive-through check-in, tables and walk-in queues, and diner points rewards. Pick: Use for dining out, configurable restaurant orders or a restaurant's tables and walk-in queue. Restaurant reservations and waitlists alone do not need booking or places. Not meals cooked at home (kitchen), ordinary bakery or shop pre-orders (commerce), or a business's client book (customers).
- dispatch: Independent courier or gig driver operations: go online by zone, accept timed offers, verify pickup and dropoff, and see shift payout breakdowns. Pick: Use for a worker handling live delivery jobs, not staff rosters (team), customer parcel maps (places), passenger ride tracking (navigation), or bookkeeping (books).
- events: Running one event from the organiser's side and the guest's: who is invited and coming, what they will eat, where they sit, who supplies what and what it costs, tickets and the door on the day, the gift list, and finding a date that suits everyone. Weddings, parties, reunions, fundraisers, small conferences. Pick: Organising one gathering: guests, RSVPs, seating, tickets, suppliers, gifts. Not travel (trips)
- fantasy: Fantasy leagues and player-stat contests: snake drafts, fantasy lineups, waiver bids, live fantasy matchups, prop picks, odds boards and pick slips. Pick: Use when managers draft real players into fantasy rosters or predict player outcomes. Not running a real sports league (sports), or a casual tabletop game (play).
- health: The most-asked personal app family: logging workouts set by set, taking medication on time, watching a body measurement move toward a goal, keeping several healthy habits, tracking symptoms, vitals and a menstrual cycle. Everything stays on the phone; nothing here is medical advice, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The body: workouts, medication, measurements, symptoms, cycles. Not the mind (mind), not food (kitchen)
- hiring: Before someone joins a team, a small employer tracks openings and applicants, reviews evidence, arranges interviews and records offers. A job seeker tracks the same process from the other side. Both can keep records on one phone; this pack does not promise a job board, shared recruiting system or automatic hiring. Pick: Finding people or work: job posts, applicants, interviews, offers and your own applications. Not staff already hired (team), not clients (customers), not a generic kanban (data)
- home: The work of a home shared among the people in it: chores and whose turn it is, rewards for kids, the family's week, recurring care for pets, plants, the car and the house, a baby's feeds and sleeps, and the devices in the rooms, including set points, one-tap scenes and sensor readings. Pick: Running a household: chores, family, pets, plants, cars, the house and its devices. Not a business team (team)
- inventory: Knowing what you have, where it is, who has it, when its warranty ends and what you still want, from a garage of boxes to a small shop's stock room, a record collection or a few rental flats. For rentals it covers the listing, the lease and a single rental-repair summary only; any request workflow (queue, triage, thread, work order) belongs to the requests pack. The tenants themselves are customers. Pick: Keeping track of things owned: stock, collections, storage, loans, warranties, rentals. Not selling them (commerce)
- invest: Following money set aside for the future: what is owned, how its value changes apart from contributions, what income it pays, and how close it brings a savings target. It records investments, not advice or orders to a broker. A first showcase uses local records and dated quotes; live prices need a service. Pick: Investments over time: holdings, allocation, watchlists, performance, dividends, savings goals. Not day-to-day spending and bills (money), not a business's books (books, proposed)
- kids: Child-facing experiences for pre-readers: profile avatars, sounds and phonics, illustrated read-alongs, stickers, visual routines and parent gates. Pick: Use kids alone for a young child's icon-first experience, even when an adult unlocks settings or the child follows a visual routine. Not graded lessons (learning), parent-managed logs and screen limits (parenting), or family chore management (home).
- kitchen: Everything about food in a household: cooking from a recipe with the right amounts and timers, planning the week's meals, the shopping list that follows from it, what is in the cupboard and when it goes off, and a simple log of what was eaten. Pick: Food at home: recipes, meal plans, groceries, the pantry, food logs. Not selling food (commerce)
- learning: Learning something step by step and checking it stuck: lessons, questions with feedback, flashcards with spaced review, a path through units, results and badges, and a student's week of classes and homework. Pick: Teaching and practising: lessons, quizzes, flashcards, classes and homework. Not a team's training rota (team)
- marketplace: Peer-to-peer resale, auctions, negotiated offers, seller bundles, hosted drops and shipping labels for secondhand sellers. Not a fixed-price retail storefront (commerce), used-car search (auto), or live-event ticket resale (ticketing).
- media: A library of things to read, hear or watch: articles, books, podcasts, albums, sermons, video courses. The core Player plays one recording; this pack adds what a library needs around it: the reading view, a show's page, episode lists, chapters, a player that follows the person between screens, and saved highlights. Pick: Reading, listening and watching a library. Not one recording on one screen (core Player)
- medical: Patient portal, pharmacy and clinical workflows: lab reference ranges, prescription refills and prices, telehealth, insurance coverage, care records and connected therapy summaries. Not personal exercise, symptom or pill tracking (health), or nonclinical client billing (customers).
- mind: Looking after how one feels: a daily check-in of mood and what affected it, a journal, naming feelings, breathing exercises, sleep, calming sounds, and the patterns that show up over weeks. It is calm by design: soft presets, no red alarms, nothing competitive. Pick: The mind: mood, journaling, feelings, breathing, sleep. Not the body (health)
- money: Personal and household money: what is in each account, where it went, what is due, who owes whom, how to clear debts, and how a holding is doing. It never moves money in a first showcase; bank links and payments are service, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The person's own money: balances, budgets, bills, splitting costs, debts and repayment plans. Not a business's sales (commerce)
- navigation: Active routing and mobility: turn-by-turn and lane guidance, route alternatives, transit legs, road hazards, trail elevation, offline maps and passenger ride tracking. Pick: Use navigation alone to compare routes, follow turn-by-turn directions on bike or foot, or make transit transfers. A destination, stop or hazard on that route does not need places. Choose places only for a separate venue, departure-board or parcel-map workflow. Not holiday itineraries (trips) or a driver's job offers (dispatch).
- news: Follow journalism and developing stories with attributed headlines, comparisons across outlets, live blogs, breaking tickers, daily digests and publisher follows. Pick: Use for discovering and following current reporting, not personal updates (social), a personal library of already saved newsletters, books or audio (media), or an enduring encyclopedia (reference).
- paperwork: IDs, insurance, tax evidence, certificates and personal contracts, with action dates and proof files. The pack is a local filing cabinet, not a bank, travel wallet, warranty book or client-consent workflow. Its hand-drawn signature pad for personal forms does not promise legally verified e-signing. - parenting: Parent-facing pregnancy, pediatric growth, co-parenting and child wellbeing: gestational milestones, growth percentiles, custody swaps, child expenses, screen limits and private family albums.
